# SOP-P1-L4-03 First-article inspection - Heat Treat line

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P1, line P1-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-CN01, EQ-P1-L4-HP02, EQ-P1-L4-HT03  
Related: ECN-2026-002, ECN-2026-007, SB-1012

1. Purpose and scope  
1.1 Purpose: Define the approved first-article inspection (FAI) workflow for incoming production runs routed through the Heat Treat line at P1-L4. This procedure applies to first-article pieces requiring turning, forging and heat-treatment operations on equipment EQ-P1-L4-CN01, EQ-P1-L4-HP02 and EQ-P1-L4-HT03.  
1.2 Scope: Use this SOP for verification of dimen­sions, surface condition, hardness records, equipment set-up confirmations and traceability prior to release of the first-article lot into continuous production.

2. Background and rationale  
2.1 Background: First-article inspection prevents propagation of process or tooling errors downstream. This SOP combines machine set-up verification, sample measurement and process record retention to provide a documented gateway for production release.  
2.2 Rationale: Key controls include machine set-up confirmation on the CNC turning center, lubrication verification for the press, and heat-treatment cycle traceability. Example failure modes addressed: incorrect chuck clamping, improper press lubrication, and missing heat-treatment records. See ECN-2026-002 for recent tooling updates and ECN-2026-007 for updated fixture drawings. SB-1012 provides sampling acceptance criteria and reporting templates.

3. Preconditions (required before executing steps)  
3.1 Materials and documentation: First-article sample, routing sheet, approved drawing, and sampling form from SB-1012 must be present.  
3.2 Responsible personnel: Qualified setup technician and FAI inspector assigned and available.  
3.3 Equipment readiness: Verify equipment identity matches list: EQ-P1-L4-CN01, EQ-P1-L4-HP02, EQ-P1-L4-HT03. Do not proceed if identification tags do not match.  
3.4 Visual check: Machine guards in place and safety interlocks show normal status. If faults are present, stop and notify Maintenance.

4. Personal protective equipment (PPE)  
4.1 Required PPE: safety glasses, cut-resistant gloves, hearing protection, and steel-toe footwear. Ensure PPE is worn whenever interacting with machines or handling hot or sharp parts.

5. Step-by-step procedure (numbered actions)  
5.1 Setup verification — EQ-P1-L4-CN01 (CNC turning center)  
5.1.1 Confirm chuck mounting and jaw seating per fixture drawing. Verify chuck jaw bolt torque for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is 90 N·m. Document the torque reading on the FAI form.  
5.1.2 Install first-article blank and conduct a dry-fit with coolant off. Inspect for runout and secure fit. Record any deviations and corrective actions taken.  
5.2 Lubrication verification — EQ-P1-L4-HP02 (hydraulic forging press)  
5.2.1 Confirm lubricant used in pump/reservoir matches part number listed on maintenance cards: lubricant part number for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02) is CFW-LUB-195. Note batch or container ID on the FAI form.  
5.2.2 Inspect visible seals and fittings for leaks and verify pump fill level visually against sight glass. Log observations. If leakage is detected, tag equipment and call Maintenance.  
5.3 First-article machining pass  
5.3.1 Perform a programmed cycle or manual supervised cut to produce the first-article part. Measure critical dimensions called out on the drawing and SB-1012 sampling form. Use calibrated gauges and record values.  
5.3.2 If a dimension falls outside the drawing callout, stop and follow containment per ECN-2026-002. Document the nonconformance and corrective action, including tooling change or program update.  
5.4 Forging verification — EQ-P1-L4-HP02  
5.4.1 Feed the machined blank to the press following standard material handling. Verify part orientation and die seating. Monitor first stroke for proper material flow and absence of flash beyond expected condition. Record visual assessment.  
5.5 Heat-treatment confirmation — EQ-P1-L4-HT03  
5.5.1 Place first-article part into the heat-treat batch with traceable tags. Confirm the batch log contains operator initials and part identifiers. Use the furnace/oven recorder output as the primary record. Attach a copy of the record to the FAI packet.  
5.6 Post-process inspection and sampling  
5.6.1 Measure final critical features identified in SB-1012. Perform hardness test and compare to drawing requirements. Log instrument ID and calibration status.  
5.6.2 Surface condition: inspect for scale, decarb, cracking or distortion. Photograph any anomalies and include images in the FAI packet.

6. Examples and acceptable responses  
6.1 Example 1: If the chuck jaw bolt reads 90 N·m and part runout is within tolerance, document “Torque verified; runout acceptable; proceed to machining.”  
6.2 Example 2: If lubricant container labeled CFW-LUB-195 is not available, document “Lubricant mismatch; stop process; request Maintenance review per ECN-2026-007.” Include container label photograph.

7. Records to keep and retention  
7.1 FAI packet: completed FAI form from SB-1012, torque log, lubricant container ID, dimensional measurement sheets, hardness report, furnace/oven recorder output, photographs of defects and corrective action log.  
7.2 Attachments: copies of any ECN referenced corrective actions (ECN-2026-002, ECN-2026-007).  
7.3 Retention: retain the packet in the document control system index under SOP-P1-L4-03 for audit traceability. Ensure packets are signed and dated in the sign-off section.

8. Nonconformance and escalation  
8.1 For any out-of-tolerance dimension, lubrication discrepancy or machine fault, stop the line and enter a hold note in production control. Notify Quality and Maintenance. Escalate per ECN-2026-002 if tooling change is required.

9. Sign-off (required)  
9.1 Setup technician: name, signature, time, confirm items 5.1 through 5.2 completed.  
9.2 FAI inspector: name, signature, time, confirm items 5.3 through 5.6 completed and records attached.  
9.3 Production manager: name, signature, date, approve release to continuous production.

10. Notes and references  
10.1 See ECN-2026-002 for tooling and chucking-related engineering changes.  
10.2 See ECN-2026-007 for maintenance and fixture amendments.  
10.3 Use SB-1012 for sampling forms and FAI packet templates.
